title: Shopify Rebellion Gold sweep SK Nebula to book KRÜ Blaze clash
content:
Shopify Rebellion Gold have moved one step closer to the VALORANT Game Changers Championship 2026 title after defeating SK Nebula 2-0 in São Paulo.

The North American roster won the upper-bracket quarterfinal on October 24 and will now face VISA KRÜ Blaze in the upper semifinals on October 27. The victory extends Shopify Rebellion Gold’s winning streak to six consecutive series and keeps the team on the safer side of the double-elimination bracket.

SK Nebula, meanwhile, drop into the lower bracket and will need to survive elimination matches to continue their run.

Shopify Rebellion Gold entered the matchup in excellent form.

Before arriving in Brazil, the roster had won its final five series in Game Changers North America Stage 2. That run included victories over Axolotl, HIMMERS, SwimTrek Blue and two wins against FlyQuest RED.

The 2-0 result over SK Nebula makes it six straight series victories.

title: Wo0t, Meteor and keiko headline early VALORANT off-season shake-up
content:
The 2026 VALORANT season has barely ended, but the first major roster changes are already reshaping the VCT landscape ahead of 2027. Wo0t has left Team Heretics after a three-year run, Meteor is preparing to move on from T1, and keiko has been allowed to explore options after one season with NRG.

The moves arrive before a key period in the VCT contract calendar and suggest that several major organizations are already preparing significant rebuilds for next season.

Team Heretics officially confirmed the departure of Mert “Wo0t” Alkan on October 21, ending one of the most important player tenures in the organization’s VALORANT history.

The Turkish player joined Heretics in late 2023 and became a central part of the roster during its rise into the top level of international VALORANT.

His time with Heretics included multiple international appearances, an EMEA title and deep runs on the global stage. One of his strongest individual performances came at Masters Shanghai 2024, where Heretics reached the Grand Final and Wo0t finished the event with the highest kill total.

His departure also comes amid wider changes within the roster.

title: How Many GTA 6 Pre-Orders Have Been Sold? Every Estimate So Far
content:
Around 6.45 million. That is the latest estimate of how many GTA 6 pre-orders have been sold, and it comes from analytics firm Sensor Tower, not from Rockstar. The figure covers digital pre-orders on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S up to October 20, 2026, and puts revenue at roughly $630 million with less than four weeks left before the November 19 launch.

Take-Two has not shared a single official unit number. So every count you have seen online traces back to Sensor Tower’s tracker, which has been updated in steps since pre-orders opened on June 25. Below, we have lined up every estimate in order, worked out what the pace means for launch week, and separated what is confirmed from what is modelled.

Sensor Tower’s most recent estimate puts GTA 6 at about 6.45 million digital pre-orders and $630 million in revenue as of October 20, 2026. The PS5 accounts for about 4.8 million of those copies ($468 million), and Xbox Series X|S for about 1.66 million ($162 million). That is a 74/26 split in Sony’s favour.

One week earlier, on October 13, the same tracker had GTA 6 at just over 6 million units and about $594 million. That jump of roughly 370,000 copies in seven days shows demand still building as launch gets closer.

Our first report on these numbers, GTA 6 pre-orders crossing an estimated $630 million , covers the revenue side in detail. This page tracks the unit count over time and will be updated as new data lands.

Every public number below comes from Sensor Tower’s Video Game Insights data, as published by the firm or relayed by its analysts. These are digital storefront estimates. Rockstar and Take-Two have confirmed none of them.

title: FFMAI 2026 Fall Grand Finals: Teams, Champion Rush, Prize Pool and How to Watch
content:
The FFMAI 2026 Fall Grand Finals go live today, October 25, at 5:30 PM IST, and twelve teams from six countries will play under Champion Rush rules until somebody earns the title with a Booyah. The first-place cheque is $15,000 from a $50,000 pool, and four Indian squads are still alive heading into the final day of the Free Fire MAX Asia Invitational.

Vietnam’s P Esports tops the field after a 221-point group stage. Bigetron by Vitality, the Summer champion, arrives fourth without a single Booyah to its name. India’s Team Apex Gaming, fresh off a second straight FFMIC crown, sits sixth. Here is who made it, how the finale works, what the money looks like and where to watch.

The road started on October 16 with the South Asia Play-ins, where 18 teams from India, Bangladesh, Pakistan and Nepal fought for seven Main Event spots. Those seven joined 11 invited sides from Thailand, Indonesia, Vietnam, Malaysia, India, Bangladesh, Pakistan and Nepal. If you missed the early stages, our FFMAI 2026 Fall South Asia Play-ins guide covers the groups and how the qualifiers were decided.

The Group Stage then ran from October 22 to 24. Eighteen teams were split into three groups of six, each team played 12 matches, and the top 12 on the overall table moved on. The bottom six went home. You can read how the groups were drawn in our FFMAI 2026 Fall Group Stage preview .

Group Stage points do not carry into the finale. Every team starts the Grand Finals on zero, so P Esports’ 44-point cushion over second place is gone the moment the first plane takes off. The table still tells you who arrives in form.

Champion Rush is the finals system Garena now uses across its big Free Fire events. Teams score normally for placement and eliminations until one of them reaches 110 points. That team becomes “Champion Rush eligible”. From the next match onwards, the first eligible team to win a Booyah is crowned champion, and the event ends right there.

title: Sony Steps Up PS5 Jailbreak Crackdown: Hacked Consoles Lose PSN Access Without Firmware 14.10
content:
Sony is making life harder for anyone running a jailbroken PS5. Since mid-October, consoles on firmware older than 14.10 can no longer sign in to PlayStation Network, and owners of modified systems now face a simple choice: update and lose the jailbreak, or stay on old firmware and play offline. At least one ban has been reported, and fresh reports suggest traces of a hack can survive a console reset.

The fallout reaches past the homebrew crowd. Anyone buying a used PS5 right now could end up with a console that was modified by its previous owner.

The cat-and-mouse game moved fast over about four weeks.

It worked on every firmware version except 14.00, and Reddit users said it could run recent games like Marvel’s Wolverine. Two days later, Sony shipped 14.10. We covered what that update changed in our PS5 26.06-14.10.00 patch notes , though Sony’s own changelog only mentions general security and stability fixes.

The key change is on Sony’s servers. Modified PS5 consoles can no longer connect to PSN without firmware 14.10. A post on the r/ps5homebrew subreddit showed even consoles on 14.00 being refused.

title: MIBR Benches Entire Valorant Roster, aspas and zekken Now Open to Transfers
content:
MIBR has moved its whole Valorant roster to inactive status, putting Erick “aspas” Santos, Zachary “zekken” Patrone, Andrew “Verno” Maust, Roberto “Mazino” Rivas and Ian “tex” Botsch on the market ahead of VCT 2027. The Brazilian organization announced the move on X on October 23, 2026, less than a week after it was reported as one of eight VCT Americas partner teams for the next two-year cycle.

The players are still under contract. Any club that wants one of them has to negotiate a transfer with MIBR directly.

MIBR’s statement was posted in Portuguese. According to Insider Gaming’s translation, the club said it made the decision after talks with the players’ representatives and because of “significant changes to the competitive structure” planned for 2027, including what it called a regional transition and the challenges that come with it.

The statement adds that “all existing contractual obligations remain in effect, and any potential transfers will be negotiated directly with MIBR.” In other words, these players aren’t free agents. A team that wants aspas or zekken will probably have to pay a buyout.

The staff stays. VLR.gg lists fRoD as head coach, Happy as assistant coach and Nandinnn as manager, and none of them were part of the announcement.

The key detail is the new regional setup. Sheep Esports reports that VCT Americas will run four divisions in 2027: North America, LATAM North, LATAM South and Brazil. LOUD and MIBR are the two partner teams placed in Brazil.

title: PS5 Sales Jump 22% in the US as Marvel’s Wolverine Tops September Charts Ahead of GTA 6
content:
PS5 sales in the United States rose 22% year over year in September 2026, according to Circana data shared by analyst Mat Piscatella on October 22. Dollar sales climbed even faster, up 43%. That made the PS5 the best-selling console of the month in both units and revenue, and it happened during the same five-week window in which Marvel’s Wolverine launched and the hype for GTA 6 kept building.

So which one moved the needle? Probably both. The numbers give a clearer answer than you might expect, though, and they also say a lot about what November could look like for Sony, Microsoft and Nintendo.

Circana’s September period ran for five weeks, from August 30 to October 3, 2026. All figures are US-only projections, and the hardware comparisons are against the same period in 2025.

The gap between units and dollars is the interesting part. PS5 revenue grew roughly twice as fast as the number of consoles sold, which means each buyer spent a lot more. Tech Insider, working from the Circana breakdown, puts the average PS5 price paid at about $646, up 17%. Kotaku notes that an all-digital PS5 now costs $600 in the US. People are paying more per box and still buying.

Overall US spending on games, hardware and accessories slipped 1% to $4.8 billion for the period, as Kotaku reported . Year to date, spending sits at $41.0 billion, 3% behind 2025.

One month earlier the picture looked grim. In Circana’s August 2026 report, PlayStation hardware units fell 11% and hit their lowest August since 2013, while Xbox dropped 31%, according to Gaming.net’s breakdown of Piscatella’s data. The average console price in the US was also at a record high. Piscatella said at the time that price sensitivity was becoming a real problem.

title: Worlds 2026 : KOI et Gen.G intouchables, première défaite pour la Karmine Corp
content:
Après leur exploit face à Bilibili Gaming, Movistar KOI a confirmé sa grande forme en dominant CTBC Flying Oyster. Les Espagnols ont notamment pu compter sur un Elyoya impérial dans la jungle, auteur d’un 7/2/9 sur Qiyana, pour décrocher leur deuxième succès consécutif. Avec un bilan de 2-0, KOI n’est désormais plus qu’à une victoire des playoffs. De son côté, G2 Esports a évité le piège brésilien face à LOS, au terme d’une rencontre bien plus disputée que prévu. Malgré une prestation exceptionnelle de SkewMond sur Lee Sin (10/1/8), les Samouraïs ont dû batailler près de 40 minutes pour s’imposer et revenir à 1-1.

Je pleure le niveau de Skewmond pic.twitter.com/gG48uA6Y0w

La soirée a été moins heureuse pour la Karmine Corp, battue pour la première fois de ces Worlds par LYON. Pourtant bien entrés dans leur rencontre, les Français ont progressivement subi la montée en puissance de la composition nord-américaine. Le Galio de Dhokla s’est révélé infranchissable, tandis que Syndra et Yunara ont fait la différence dans les combats d’équipe. Invaincue depuis le Play-In, la KC concède ainsi son premier revers et redescend à 1-1, alors que LYON rejoint KOI parmi les quatre équipes encore invaincues.

On y aura cru jusqu'au bout pic.twitter.com/Z7nftlm36k

Opposés à l’un de leurs principaux rivaux pour le titre mondial, les coéquipiers de Chovy ont livré une véritable démonstration, conclue sur le score de 22-7 en seulement 29 minutes. Canyon et Duro ont particulièrement brillé, permettant à Gen.G de confirmer son statut de grand favori. L’autre duel coréen a réservé davantage de suspense : malgré un bon début de partie, T1 a fini par céder face à Dplus KIA, qui a renversé la rencontre autour de l’Elder Dragon après 41 minutes de jeu. ShowMaker et ses coéquipiers rejoignent ainsi Gen.G, KOI et LYON à 2-0.

title: La Coupe de France Slash est de retour sur Rocket League
content:
La Coupe de France Slash de Rocket League s’apprête à faire son grand retour pour une deuxième édition. Après avoir attiré 1,8 million de vues en direct cumulées en 2025, l’événement renouvelle son partenariat avec France Télévisions et sa plateforme Slash. L’an dernier, Gentle Mates avait remporté le trophée face à la Karmine Corp lors de la finale organisée à la Paris Games Week. Cette fois, la compétition se déroulera entièrement en ligne et permettra aux nouvelles compositions de se mesurer avant la reprise du circuit professionnel.

Le tournoi se tiendra du 28 octobre au 12 novembre, avec une diffusion exclusive des phases de poule du 2 au 11 novembre, avant les demi-finales et la grande finale programmées le 12 novembre. L’ensemble des rencontres sera accessible gratuitement sur les chaînes Twitch et YouTube de Slash, ainsi que sur ses comptes X et TikTok. Les commentaires seront assurés par RocketBaguette, collectif incontournable de la scène francophone Rocket League.

Avec cette deuxième édition, France Télévisions confirme sa volonté de renforcer la visibilité de l’esport auprès du grand public. La Coupe de France Slash constituera également un premier rendez-vous intéressant pour observer les nouveaux effectifs de la scène française, dans un mercato particulièrement mouvementé à l’approche des RLCS 2027.

title: flameZ climbs out of a 0-8 hole on Cache to take apEX-less Vitality past 9z 2-0
content:
ZywOo and flameZ both started Cache 0-8 and Vitality fell 4-7 behind on their own map pick, then won it 13-10 to finish a 2-0 series in which jL took the first of five steps towards a Major sticker.

For nine rounds of Cache, ZywOo did not register a kill. flameZ had also started the map 0-8. It was the map Team Vitality had picked, one they had won seven of their previous eight times, and 9z led 6-2 on it.

Vitality still won it 13-10. flameZ finished Cache with 22 kills, 13 deaths and 100.2 ADR, almost all of it on the CT side after the break, and the 2-0 win over 9z gives the top seed a clean start at PGL Masters Bucharest 2026 in their first series without apEX .

Cache was supposed to be ZywOo’s map, and Vitality went into the series with an 88% win rate on it over the previous three months. 9z took that away early. They won the pistol round, went 4-0 up and never let Vitality break their control of mid, which left the attack with little but direct hits on the sites, straight into 9z’s layered setups.

ZywOo’s first kill came in round 10, and it came as a triple that won a round 9z had set up perfectly. Vitality were still 4-7 down a round later and went into the half at 5-7, kept in touch by ropz, who repeatedly led them onto the B site and won the duels that opened it.

The CT side was a different map. Vitality won the second pistol round, and flameZ took over the middle of the map on the rounds that followed as Vitality levelled at 7-7 and went ahead. When HUASOPEEK won a one-against-three post-plant to tie the map at 9-9, a clutch that broke Vitality’s economy and handed 9z a 10-9 lead on the following round, flameZ answered with a triple from A main, alone against two players coming through the squeaky door, to level it again. jL’s double kill made it 11-10, and ZywOo’s triple against 9z’s pistols took Vitality to map point. ZywOo, who had been 0-8, ended Cache 15-14. Vitality won the last four rounds.

title: syph0 drags Nemiga through four overtimes in 2-0 win over Legacy
content:
Nemiga needed four overtimes and a 47-kill map from syph0 to win their own pick against last year’s Bucharest finalists, then took Dust2 13-8 for a sweep that leaves them on the edge of a Singapore Major spot.

Nemiga ‘s first match at PGL Masters Bucharest 2026 ended in a sweep of Legacy . Ancient, their own pick, ran to a fourth overtime before they took it 25-23, and Legacy’s Dust2 followed 13-8.

Legacy came in as clear favourites. They are eighth in Valve’s Regional Standings, reached the final in Bucharest a year ago, where they lost 3-2 to Aurora, and their Major place was never in doubt. Nemiga were 23rd and came through the European closed qualifier. For them, this was the match that mattered most of the whole event. Before the series, HLTV’s simulation gave them an 80.5% chance of an invite to the PGL Major Singapore, rising to 96.9% with a win.

The series was decided on a map that refused to end. Ancient is Nemiga’s most played map, and they had it won several times over. They led 12-9 and had three map points in regulation. Legacy saved all three and kept going, six rounds in a row in all, to stand on map point themselves at 15-12 in the first overtime. Nemiga came back to force a second overtime, then a third, then a fourth.

Legacy survived on clutches. latto won three of them on the map and dumau two, and every time Nemiga looked ready to close, a Legacy player on low health found another headshot. Nemiga’s habit of forcing the pace, which won them rounds early, became predictable deep into the overtimes, and Legacy started to wait for the fights to come to them.

Nemiga still found the answers when it counted. Xant3r, quiet for most of the map, won a one-against-two by sitting on the bomb when nobody expected him there. In the fourth overtime Legacy saved one more map point at 24-22, before Nemiga finally closed it out 25-23 in round 48.

title: BetBoom stun world number one Spirit 2-1 as zorte’s AWP clutch ends Mirage in overtime
content:
BetBoom beat Team Spirit 13-3 on Spirit’s own Ancient pick, came back from 4-8 on Mirage and closed the series with a one-against-three from zorte, while donk had one of the worst series of his year.

Team Spirit arrived at PGL Masters Bucharest 2026 as the top-ranked team in the world on HLTV and lost their first match 2-1 to BetBoom on Saturday. Spirit won BetBoom’s pick Anubis 13-10, but BetBoom answered with 13-3 on Ancient and a 16-14 overtime win on Mirage.

Spirit arrived as the number one team in the world on HLTV and clear favourites. BetBoom came straight from Malta, where they lost the Thunderpick World Championship final 2-3 to FURIA last Sunday after leading the series 2-1. Bucharest was their chance to show that Malta was not a one-off. They leave the first day with the biggest scalp in the tournament.

The last round of the series belonged to zorte. BetBoom had two map points in regulation, at 12-10 and 12-11, and two more in overtime at 15-13 and 15-14. Spirit saved the first three. On the fourth, zorte was left alone with an AWP against three Spirit players. He killed one with a no-scope, switched to his pistol and finished the other two to close Mirage 16-14.

It capped his best series in a long time. He finished with 57 kills and 37 deaths, the most kills and the best K-D in the match by a distance, and 87% KAST. On Ancient he went 14-4 with 106.2 ADR. zorte had not put up big numbers for some time before Malta, but he was one of BetBoom’s best players there, and in Bucharest he carried that over against the best team in the world.

He was not alone. Every BetBoom player except Boombl4 and Magnojez finished with more kills than deaths, and the in-game leader made up for his numbers with the calling. Boombl4 had ten kills before Spirit won a single round on Ancient. He also outcalled magixx over the series, most clearly on Ancient, and kept BetBoom calm when the decider slipped into overtime.

title: VCT EMEA : nAts a fait son choix, Team Liquid garde son capitaine

title: Liquid upset MOUZ 2-1 with a different hero on every map
content:
Team Liquid beat ESL Pro League finalists MOUZ in the first round of the Swiss stage after their in-game leader went from 10 kills on Ancient to 26 on Inferno, and a different Liquid player stepped up on every map.

MOUZ arrived in Bucharest as ESL Pro League finalists and lost their first match at PGL Masters Bucharest 2026 2-1 to Team Liquid . MOUZ took their own pick, Ancient, 16-13 in overtime, but Liquid swept the overtime on Inferno to win it 16-12 and closed the series 13-11 on Mirage.

Few first round results looked less likely on paper. MOUZ are second in Valve’s Regional Standings and reached the ESL Pro League Season 24 final two weeks ago, where they lost 0-3 to Vitality. Liquid came to Bucharest as North America’s qualifier, 24th in the VRS, and on a run of three straight series losses, two of them 0-2 at 1win Private Club Season 2 earlier this week. They were heavy underdogs.

Ancient was the map Liquid should have won, and the one JT will want to forget. The South African in-game leader finished it with 10 kills and 21 deaths. Liquid still led 6-2 and 8-5, won the first half 7-5, before MOUZ took control and went 12-9 up.

NAF kept the map alive almost on his own. He won a round with a triple kill, EliGE killed the defuser in a post-plant clutch to make it 11-12, and NAF then won a one-against-five to force overtime, the second 1v5 clutch of his career. MOUZ won overtime 4-1.

On Inferno, Liquid’s pick, JT was a different player. He went 26-14 with 80.9 ADR, the most kills on the map, and he was the standout player. His calling held up too. Liquid won the first five rounds, then lost seven in a row to trail 5-7 at the half. They recovered to lead 12-9 with three map points, lost all three, and still won all four rounds of overtime, with a four-kill round from JT in the middle of it.

title: Aurora’s title defence starts with a 2-1 loss to The MongolZ
content:
The MongolZ lost their own map pick in overtime, then won Aurora’s Nuke 13-2 and closed the series on Dust2, two days after lifting their first trophy in 14 months.

Defending champions Aurora are 0-1 at PGL Masters Bucharest 2026 after a 2-1 loss to The MongolZ on Saturday morning. Aurora took Inferno 16-12 in overtime, but The MongolZ hit back with 13-2 on Nuke and 13-9 on Dust2.

The MongolZ came in as clear underdogs. Aurora are fifth in Valve’s Regional Standings, have finished in the top three at each of their last three events and won this tournament a year ago. The MongolZ were 23rd, playing at 09:00 in Bucharest after a grand final in Belgrade on Thursday night, and with a lineup that has been together for less than three weeks.

Inferno was The MongolZ’ pick, and for a long time it looked like the map they would lose the series on. They won the pistol and led 4-1, but Aurora won six rounds in a row and went into the half 7-5 up. In the second half Aurora reached 12-9 with three map points, before The MongolZ won three straight rounds to force overtime.

There, Aurora were the better team. Wicadia, who finished Inferno with 26 kills and 108.2 ADR, had five kills in the last two rounds, and at 13-12 Jimpphat won a two-against-three round on B by waiting inside a smoke with the AWP. Aurora won overtime 4-0.

Losing your own map pick after saving three map points is the kind of result that can end a series. It was the one scenario The MongolZ could not afford: with Nuke, one of their weakest maps, coming next, they had to win Inferno.

Cette fois, 3XA devrait retrouver un visage familier : SlowQ, avec qui il avait remporté le Summer Split de LFL et les EMEA Masters sous les couleurs de la Karmine Corp Blue en 2025. Le midlaner coréen, sous contrat jusqu’en novembre 2027, devrait être conservé par SK Gaming, qui souhaite construire son nouvel effectif autour de ce duo.

Ce retour au plus haut niveau intervient après une année 2026 particulièrement mouvementée pour 3XA. Malgré son sacre européen avec KCB en 2025, l’ADC n’avait pas réussi à retrouver une place en LEC lors du précédent mercato. Il avait finalement rejoint French Flair en LFL, avant de poursuivre la saison chez Joblife. Une aventure également écourtée, puisque le joueur avait demandé à quitter l’équipe en plein Summer Split après des performances décevantes. Alors que plusieurs ADC prometteurs des ligues régionales, notamment Harpoon et Aetinoth, sont également susceptibles de rejoindre l’élite européenne, 3XA aurait accepté une proposition rapidement formulée par SK Gaming.

L’organisation allemande prépare de son côté une reconstruction majeure après une nouvelle saison ratée. Onzième du LEC Versus, puis huitième des Spring et Summer Splits, SK Gaming n’a toujours pas retrouvé les playoffs depuis l’été 2024. Les contrats de Wunder, Skeanz, Jopa et Mikyx arrivent tous à expiration en novembre, tandis que Jopa explore déjà ses possibilités ailleurs. Avec SlowQ et 3XA comme premières pièces de son projet 2027, SK espère retrouver une compétitivité qui lui échappe depuis plusieurs saisons. Reste désormais à connaître les trois autres joueurs qui viendront compléter cet effectif.

FUT Esports opened PGL Masters Bucharest 2026 with a 2-0 win over TYLOO on Saturday morning, taking Nuke 13-9 and Ancient 13-6 in the first round of the Swiss stage.

The result was what everyone expected. FUT are tenth in Valve’s Regional Standings, TYLOO 59th, and FUT had already beaten them twice this year. How FUT got there was less certain. The series was the first official match for SunPayus , who joined as the team’s primary AWPer on 1 October after his release from G2 and took over the role from cmtry . FUT had not played since a 0-2 loss to Vitality at BLAST Open Porto on 31 August, and for half a map it showed.

FUT takes down TYLOO in Stream B @futesportsgg win 2-0 and move to 1W-0L, while @tyloogaming fall to 0W-1L #PGLMasters pic.twitter.com/dNNtajZFSD

TYLOO picked Nuke, a map where FUT had won only one of four in the previous three months, and for the first ten rounds the pick looked inspired. Zero, the player to watch for TYLOO before the match, was the engine, and he finished Nuke with 17 kills and a team-high 80.9 ADR.

SunPayus was the one part of FUT’s defence that held. He started the half quietly, but once he settled outside and in lockers with the AWP, TYLOO’s attacks began to stall. title: BIG sign up for EPIC.LAN in late push for a Major spot

BIG appeared on EPIC.LAN’s team list on Friday evening, with one player added so far. It is a bring-your-own-computer event, and every player needs a £95 participant ticket. EPIC.LAN says the event meets Valve’s requirements to count in the rankings, provided HLTV covers it.

The German organisation need the points. They finished third at 1win Private Club Season 2 after losing the lower bracket final to The MongolZ on Thursday, a result that, as Pley reported at the time , left them needing a near-perfect run at Stake Ranked.

Valve’s ranking model, published on GitHub, rates teams on their own prize money, on the prize money of the teams they beat and how many teams those opponents have beaten, and on their ten best LAN wins, alongside head-to-head results. The opponent factors are scaled by each event’s prize pool. The LAN factor is not: a recent win on LAN counts the same in Kettering as anywhere else.

That is the only real gain on offer, according to VRS analyst Udknud. He wrote that EPIC.LAN “has low event weight and (very) low ranked opposition, so there are only the LAN win points to gain from wins there.”

title: apEX’s Major sticker and Astralis’ invite on the line as PGL Masters Bucharest begins
content:
PGL Masters Bucharest is the last tier-one event before Valve sets the invitations for PGL Major Singapore. Beyond the $1,250,000 title, two roster questions will be settled by a simple count: Vitality need five matches with jL for him to replace apEX on their Major roster, and FUT need five with SunPayus to remove cmtry, now an Astralis player, from theirs.

The Swiss stage starts on Saturday 09:00 CEST , when FUT open against TYLOO and defending champions Aurora face The MongolZ . Sixteen teams play in PGL’s studio until the grand final on 31 October. Two days later, on 2 November, Valve’s Regional Standings decide who is invited to which stage of the Major in Singapore, which starts on 24 November.

For most of the field, the Major invite is already safe. What is still open is who goes straight to Stage 3, who has to play more rounds, and, for two teams, which five players the invitation will actually name.

Valve’s Regional Standings do not rank organisations. They rank rosters, and Valve’s published code sets out how a roster is defined. The model looks at a team’s last ten matches and includes “only the most recent players who have played five or more matches on this roster”. A team is still treated as the same team as long as at least three players carry over, so a single stand-in or signing does not reset its points.

In practice, a new player needs five of the last ten matches before he replaces the player he came in for. Until then, the name of the departed player stays on the roster that gets the invitation.

The latest official standings, published by Valve on 5 October, list Vitality as apEX, flameZ, mezii, ropz and ZywOo, and FUT as cmtry, dem0n, dziugss, Krabeni and xfl0ud. Valve’s Major Supplemental Rulebook states that “invitations will be sent to intact rosters” and that the roster a team registers “must match the invited roster”. A team may add one substitute and one coach.

title: Exclusive: MLBB at 10, From Niche Mobile MOBA to Global Esports Powerhouse
content:
Mobile Legends: Bang Bang’s (MLBB) first decade has been a roller coaster ride. What started as a game in a niche and underappreciated section of the gaming market turned into one of the biggest esports titles in the world.

Now that MLBB has gained global recognition, what’s next in line for the game? Esports.gg talked with key figures behind the mobile MOBA title to answer that question. Hailong “Q” Quan , head of MLBB Battlefield Business at MOONTON Games, reflected on the game’s decade-long evolution. Meanwhile, Ray Ng , head of the Esports Ecosystem , discussed the growth of MLBB esports and the company’s vision for global expansion.

When Hailong Quan joined the MLBB project team in 2016, the game was only in its infancy. Prominent MOBA titles like League of Legends and DOTA 2 were fighting for the top spot.

Southeast Asia presented a different opportunity: a largely untapped market for mobile gaming and esports. MLBB took the opportunity to build a community around the gaming-on-the-go culture. What began as a mobile MOBA would eventually grow into a major esports title, deeply embedded in Southeast Asian gaming culture and increasingly reaching audiences around the world.

Ten years later, Quan leads the MLBB Battlefield Business at MOONTON Games, overseeing the game’s in-match combat experience. As the title celebrates its 10th anniversary, he sees its evolution as something more personal, something akin to “celebrating a birthday with a long-time companion.”

Watching MLBB grow from its early days to where it is now fills me with such deep emotion; it’s like a father watching his child grow into an extraordinary person .

Cloud9 dispose désormais d’une base contractuelle solide pour préparer 2027. Thanatos, Blaber et Tactical sont engagés jusqu’en 2028, tandis que Loki possède un contrat courant jusqu’à fin 2027. title: « Nous sommes bien plus forts que l’an dernier » : Labrov et G2 en confiance avant les Worlds 2026
content:
Considéré comme le principal espoir occidental aux Worlds 2026, G2 Esports aborde le championnat du monde avec une confiance retrouvée. Dans une interview accordée à DPM Esports , Labros « Labrov » Papoutsakis est revenu sur la préparation de son équipe, notamment après plusieurs rumeurs concernant des résultats décevants en scrims. « Nous avons eu quelques journées où les entraînements ne se passaient pas bien, mais nous avons réussi à rebondir. Actuellement, je dirais que nous sommes vraiment très forts et que nous apprenons beaucoup. » Le support précise que G2 s’entraîne désormais régulièrement contre des équipes asiatiques et estime que l’arrivée de Perkz dans l’encadrement a également contribué à améliorer le niveau collectif. Après avoir remporté tous les titres européens cette année, les Samouraïs semblent donc prêts à relever le défi international.

Labrov estime que G2 a franchi un véritable cap depuis son élimination au MSI 2025, qui avait poussé les joueurs à revoir profondément leur manière de travailler. « Tout le monde a passé énormément d’heures à chercher comment progresser, individuellement et collectivement. C’est le jour et la nuit, alors que cela ne fait même pas un an et demi. » Le Grec souligne également l’influence de ses coéquipiers sur sa propre progression, notamment Hans Sama pour la phase de lane et Caps pour sa compréhension du jeu. Désormais comparé à Hylissang à son meilleur niveau, Labrov accueille ces rapprochements comme un compliment, lui qui admirait particulièrement l’agressivité et l’intelligence de jeu de l’ancien support de Fnatic.

Concernant les ambitions de G2, Labrov refuse de se fixer des limites, tout en restant lucide sur la difficulté du tournoi. « Soulever le trophée des Worlds serait un rêve devenu réalité pour tout le monde, et c’est mon objectif principal. » Avant de penser au titre, il souhaite toutefois franchir une première étape : sortir du Swiss Stage. « Je pense que nous sommes bien plus forts que l’année dernière et que c’est possible. Évidemment, ce ne sera pas facile, je nous donnerais peu de chances, mais je pense que nous pouvons le faire. Je ne dirais pas que nous sommes favoris, mais je suis convaincu que nous pouvons aller loin. » Un discours ambitieux mais mesuré, à quelques heures de l’entrée en lice de G2 face à Dplus KIA.

title: Moscow Game Week Returns With Global Studios and Ranked CS2 Finals
content:
Moscow International Game Week will return for its second edition from October 29 to November 1, 2026, combining an international games exhibition, industry discussions and the Moscow Cyber Games Counter-Strike 2 LAN finals. Organisers say more than 85 companies will exhibit, with participants from India, Brazil, China, South Korea and Malaysia among those announced.

The official event schedule separates the wider city programme from the main venue activities. City events begin on October 29, while the gaming exhibition and business programme run from October 30 to November 1. The main venue is Moscow Game Hub, identified on the website as the Video Games and Animation Cluster at 40 Bolshoy Boulevard.

The announced overseas exhibitors include Brazil’s national stand, Brasilia Game Hub, China’s Chingmu, South Korean companies BURNING SOUL and BEAR&SKUNK, and Malaysia’s Experimental Design Team. Together, the exhibitors cover game development, creative services and technology used in production.

Russian publishers and gaming platforms will also present their work. An indie alley will bring together independent projects, while a separate residents’ alley will feature studios based at Moscow Game Hub. According to the organisers’ announcement, visitors will be able to try games, meet their creators and learn about game and animation development. A themed merchandise marketplace is also planned.

This year’s theme, “Beyond the Industry,” focuses on the relationship between games, animation, film and literature. Discussions will examine how creators can develop fictional worlds across different formats and find partners for new projects. The programme is intended for developers, investors and professionals working in related creative fields, alongside the exhibition’s public audience.

The published business tracks cover cultural identity in game design, business development and government support, shared fictional universes, education and AI in animation. Training, internships and practical experience are included in the education strand. The agenda therefore extends from producing individual games to building studios and developing stories that can support several kinds of media.

title: South Korea’s Culture Ministry Outlines Gaming Support
content:
South Korea’s culture ministry plans to support major game development, independent studios and training for an industry adapting to AI. Culture, Sports and Tourism Minister Choi Hwi-young outlined those priorities during an October 23 parliamentary audit, acknowledging slowing growth and pressure from Chinese competitors.

According to Inven Global , he said support had been reflected in next year’s budget plans. The ministry’s published proposals show where that support would go. Its 2027 budget outline includes 43.9 billion won for game planning and production programmes covering Global Frontier projects, indie titles and other initiatives.

The proposal also places games within a wider content-industry funding programme, linking support for individual productions with the government’s broader cultural-sector ambitions.

The ministry’s 2027 budget document shows a 10.5 billion won increase for the game planning and production category. Its overall proposed content-sector budget is 1.7719 trillion won. The 43.9 billion won figure covers the specified production-support category, rather than the government’s entire gaming budget. It remains a proposed allocation, with individual awards and delivery requiring separate implementation.

At an October 20 advisory meeting, Choi gave further details of the intended support. Yonhap reported that the new Global Frontier production-support programme had been allocated 6 billion won in the proposal. Planned indie creation funding would increase from 9.3 billion won to 13.8 billion won. The ministry’s announcement of that meeting also identified young talent as a priority alongside flagship projects and independent games.

During the parliamentary audit, Choi also described preparations for training and practical experience as AI changes game production. That places workforce development alongside financial support for studios.

title: Co-streams now draw almost half of esports viewing as official broadcasts slip
content:
Community broadcasts accounted for 49.4% of all hours watched across 15 major esports tournaments that ended in the third quarter of 2026, up from 43.6% a year earlier. Official channels lost 5.4% in the same period, while Counter-Strike showed why more hours do not always mean a bigger audience.

The figures come from a new report by Esports Charts , which compared the 15 events with their 2025 editions. Co-streams grew by 19.7%, more than three times as fast as total viewing.

📺 Co-streaming grew 19.7% in Q3 2026, while official esports broadcasts lost ground. But does a bigger community audience actually mean more viewers overall? 👀 Our latest report breaks it down 👇 https://t.co/GkJGwbknJc

Co-streaming grew by more than 3% at 12 of the 15 events. Eight of them also held or grew their official viewing, while four saw the official feeds drop by more than 3%. A bigger co-stream share did not always mean a bigger audience. At the MLBB Mid Season Cup, co-stream hours rose 20.3%, but official hours fell 23.3% and the total dropped 12.6%. Esports Charts stresses that its data shows how much viewing co-streamers capture, not whether they bring in viewers who would otherwise not have watched.

Two Counter-Strike events are in the sample, and they point in different directions.

BLAST Open Fall 2026, won by Spirit after a 3-1 final against MOUZ , had the second largest increase in co-stream hours of all 15 tournaments, just behind the PUBG Mobile World Cup. Total hours and average viewers went up as well, while official watch time stayed essentially flat. The event finished with 23.7 million hours watched, 280,966 average viewers and a peak of 849,574 for the grand final, according to Esports Charts’ event page.

title: Gears of War: E-Day Reportedly Cost Over $500 Million, and Its Finished PS5 Version Never Shipped
content:
Gears of War: E-Day cost Microsoft more than $500 million to make, according to a new report , and that figure leaves out marketing. The claim surfaced on October 22, two weeks after the game launched as an Xbox console exclusive. Microsoft has not commented.

If the number holds, E-Day sits among the most expensive games ever made. It also puts fresh weight on a question fans have asked since June: why would Xbox shelve a PS5 version that was reportedly already finished?

Kotaku’s number comes from one “source familiar with Xbox’s business,” who said spending “was over $500 million, and that’s before you include marketing.” Kotaku and Forbes both asked Microsoft for comment. Neither got an answer.

Chris Dring of The Game Business backed the figure in public, saying that from what he’d been told it was “very true.” For scale, Insomniac’s Marvel’s Spider-Man 2 cost roughly $300 million, a number that only came out through the studio’s 2023 data leak.

Work on E-Day began around 2020 at The Coalition, a Vancouver studio of about 300 people, with People Can Fly helping on development. Six years of AAA production at that headcount adds up fast.

Not everyone accepts the figure. Back in June, Insider Gaming’s Tom Henderson said he’d heard the game cost “upwards of $400 million,” and Jez Corden of Windows Central pushed back hard.

title: Is Hush Actually Broken? A Deep Dive Into VALORANT’s Newest Duelist
content:
Since Riot Games officially revealed Hush, the community has been in an uproar, with many players already declaring the new telekinetic Duelist to be completely “broken.” Between her ability to manipulate weapons from afar, a highly versatile flash, and an ultimate that literally levitates enemies helplessly into the air, it is easy to see why she has sparked so much panic.

However, before we start comparing her to peak-era Chamber, we need to take a step back. While her kit boasts an incredibly high skill ceiling, a closer analysis of the gameplay footage reveals several glaring weaknesses. Here is why Hush might not be as overpowered as you think.

Hush’s passive ability, Telekinesis, allows her to interact with the environment from a distance. While this sounds game-breaking on paper, it is currently the only passive in the game tied to a strict 30-second cooldown, drastically limiting how often it can be abused.

Furthermore, its utility is highly situational.

Hush’s core utility revolves around a unique “prep and redirect” mechanic. Both her signature pull (Displacement) and her blind (Flashbulb) can be thrown out with a left-click, or prepped to sit on your screen with a right-click. Reactivating the keybind sends the utility flying toward your crosshair.

At first glance, Hush’s dash ability, Flow, seems underwhelming. You place an anchor and are pulled toward it. However, extended gameplay footage shows this ability behaving much more like a Raze Satchel than a Jett Dash. Hush carries her momentum fluidly, allowing for “extended tech” that can cover more distance and elevation than standard Duelist movement abilities.

title: Beginning to play CS2 in 2026? Here’s all you need to know
content:
Counter-Strike 2 is one of the most-played games on the planet, and one of the easiest to hear about without ever understanding. It is free. It is Valve’s tactical shooter, and under one name or another it has anchored competitive PC gaming for over two decades.

Maybe you have watched a clip, or seen a friend chase a knife worth more than their monitor, or you just want to know what the fuss is about. Either way, here is the lay of the land, from the esports down to the cosmetics.

CS2 is a five-versus-five tactical shooter, released in 2023 as the successor to the long-running CS:GO. One team tries to plant a bomb. The other defends the two bombsites and races to defuse it. Win enough rounds and you take the match, and the teams swap attack and defence at the halfway mark.

There is no respawning inside a round, so a single mistake can end it for you. Money matters too. Before each round you buy guns and armour with cash earned from the last one, so a losing streak starves you of firepower. Skill is earned through aim and positioning, never unlocked with playtime. That is the whole appeal: free to load up, brutally hard to master.

This is where plenty of newcomers arrive first. CS2 has one of the largest esports scenes in the world. Valve runs the showpiece Majors, third parties fill the rest of the calendar, and the prize money is real: the best players have banked more than two million dollars in career winnings.

Teams like Vitality and Spirit sell out arenas, and names like ZywOo, s1mple and the teenage phenomenon donk carry the sort of following footballers do. Best of all, you can watch nearly all of it free, on Twitch and YouTube, in dozens of languages, most weekends of the year. You do not need to play a single round to enjoy it. The tension of a one-versus-one with the bomb ticking needs no translation. The biggest finals pull in millions of concurrent viewers online.

title: Fortnite Wins Australian Court Battle, Reclaims Spot on iOS
content:
Fortnite returns to iOS in Australia on October 22, 2026, after the Federal Court of Australia ruled against Apple in the Epic Games antitrust case. Justice Jonathan Beach found that Apple broke competition law by limiting app distribution and payment options. Epic announced the return on X, and Apple plans to appeal. The court also ordered Apple to open iOS to third-party app stores and alternative payments by March 1, 2027.

This article covers the return date, the court ruling, the March 2027 changes, and Apple’s response.

Epic Games said on X that Fortnite would come back to the Australian App Store on Thursday, October 22. Players in Australia can now download the game straight from the App Store. Before this, they had to go through the Epic Games Store.

The return follows a ruling that Apple violated Australian competition law. The court found that Apple restricted how apps are distributed and how users pay inside them. It also ordered Apple to readmit Fortnite and other Epic apps once Epic sends a written request. Readmission stays subject to App Store rules that match the court’s orders.

Epic CEO Tim Sweeney reacted on X after the remedies were issued. He called the outcome a “huge victory for consumers and developers” and said Epic is studying the verdict. He added that more details will follow.

title: Capcom details CAPCOM ID incident: Gameplay unaffected, 196 passwords reset
content:

Capcom has confirmed only its second ever major security breach, sharing on Oct. 22 that a third party gained unauthorized access to CAPCOM ID, its unified account service, exposing 11,774,247 records worldwide. Services that use the login still work, Capcom says no credit card information was involved but 43 accounts had personal information exposed, including their date of birth. 196 accounts also had their passwords changed by the attacker.

CAPCOM ID is the single account used across Capcom's web services and select online games, including Street Fighter 6 . Anyone who plays or registers on those services holds one, and while some sources claim only Japanese accounts have been affected by this breach, others say it’s a global issue.

The leaked records consist of email addresses and system-unique identifiers, meaning data Capcom's systems log for each account. Capcom gave the figure only as a worldwide total, with no breakdown by country or region, even if many are speculating that the attack was limited to Japanese users.

Capcom found no evidence that passwords users set themselves were leaked but has warned all customers to be on their guard if “Capcom” emails them.

title: Is Japan the Weakest Region at BMIC 2026? A Look at Its International Performances
content:
Japan is one of the most established regions in PUBG Mobile esports, but its recent international performances have raised questions ahead of the BGMI International Cup (BMIC) 2026 . The tournament will take place from October 30 to November 1 in Mumbai, featuring six Indian teams, five South Korean teams, and five Japanese teams.

South Korea has been one of the strongest regions in international PUBG Mobile competitions, while Indian teams have recently started delivering better results on the global stage. However, Japan has struggled in several major tournaments over the past few years. Does this make Japan the weakest region heading into BMIC 2026? Let’s look at the results.

Japan has a long history in PUBG Mobile esports, with organisations like REJECT representing the country internationally. REJECT, which featured popular players such as SaRa and Reiji, won the PUBG Mobile Global Open (PMGO) 2024. It remains Japan’s only major global PUBG Mobile championship title.

However, the region has struggled to repeat that success. At BMIC 2025, REJECT finished at the bottom of the standings despite entering the tournament with high expectations. CAG Osaka was Japan’s best-performing team, finishing third after a strong comeback on the final day. Apart from CAG Osaka, the other three Japanese teams finished among the bottom five. While South Korean teams fought for the championship and Indian teams delivered competitive performances, most Japanese teams struggled throughout the tournament.

Japan’s struggles were also visible at the PUBG Mobile World Cup (PMWC). At PMWC 2026, Japan was represented by DOPENESS, which qualified after winning the Japanese league. However, the team struggled in the Group Stage and finished 13th, narrowly advancing to the Survival Stage. DOPENESS then finished 11th in the Survival Stage and was eliminated, ending its World Cup campaign in 21st place overall. In comparison, both Indian teams qualified for the PMWC 2026 Grand Finals.

Japan also struggled at PMWC 2025. KINOTROPE represented the region with a roster that included two South Korean players. Despite having international experience in the lineup, the team finished 23rd, or second-last, in the tournament. The situation was similar at the PUBG Mobile Global Championship (PMGC) 2025, where REJECT finished 37th overall.

title: Interview with Tencent: How esports technology shapes the future of competition in Asia
content:
The 2026 Asian Games recently concluded in Japan’s Aichi-Nagoya, and what made the competition interesting was the Olympic Council of Asia’s (OCA) inclusion of esports as an official medal event. Players duked it out in titles such as League of Legends, Mobile Legends: Bang Bang (MLBB), Street Fighter 6, TEKKEN 8, and more. Tencent Esports, the official technology partner of the OCA, sat down for an exclusive interview with esports.gg.

We spoke with Teri Zhang, senior director of Tencent’s esports business department and esports manager at the OCA, about esports’ evolution as a recognized sport, the impact of technology, and the future of competitive gaming in Asia.

Esports as a medal event is not new to the Asian Games since it first appeared in 2018 as a demonstration before the OCA added it to the 2026 Games calendar in 2023. Despite uncertainty over its inclusion in late 2024, the OCA approved the final lineup in 2025. Asian Games 2026 then featured 13 video game titles across 11 medal events.

In her interview with esports.gg, Zhang shared how this continued inclusion of esports at the Asian Games shows its growing role in the region. This growth also shifts the focus from proving that esports belongs in major sporting events to running competitions fairly and consistently at scale.

“The conversation has evolved beyond whether esports belongs at the Asian Games. The focus today is on how esports can be successfully integrated into a multi-sport environment at scale,” Zhang said, adding that the OCA must manage six competitive categories, different gaming devices, technical requirements, and more at an unprecedented level.

“In that sense, the Asian Games serves as a milestone for esports and an opportunity to strengthen the foundations that will support its long-term development,” she continued. “It allows the industry to refine competition processes, technical standards, and review mechanisms that can be applied consistently across future events.”

title: How to find and open a Safe in Modern Warfare 4 DMZ
content:
Throughout your career in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 DMZ, you’ll continually get to complete DMZ Orders, which are specific tasks that earn you rewards the more you complete them. While some of the DMZ Orders are simple, others can be rather difficult, and one of the more challenging ones is to “Open a Safe.”

While this sounds trivial at first glance, you then realize that Safes aren’t too common to find on the Hajin map in DMZ. Luckily, though, we know of some dedicated spots for Safes that allow you to complete this DMZ Order with no problem at all.

For us, this specific DMZ Order was on Page 5, and it even says that you can find Safes in Compounds and Locked Spaces . Of course, that doesn’t help a lot, as you still need to go out and search for these locations and then locate the Safe itself.

While you might have some serious trouble trying to find a “Locked Space,” you shouldn’t have many problems locating a Compound. These are marked by a tent icon on your Tac-Map and are fairly common in Hajin, particularly out in the woodlands or the side roads in between the major points of interest on the map.

In order to open a Safe in a Compound, you need to enter it and then clear out 100% of the enemy AI from the area . This is tracked by a percentage meter that appears on the left side of your screen when you enter a Compound. There are usually around 10-12 enemies in each Compound, and when they’re all cleared out, your meter will read 100%.

From here, you need to find the Safe that the Compound has stashed. For the most part, the Safe is located at the top of the guard tower, which is found at most Compounds . Just climb the stairs to get to the top, and you’ll find the Safe sitting on the ground next to a desk. Interact with it, loot the contents, and you’ll get a mission completion for this DMZ Order.

title: PHP Flaw Is Taking Gaming and Esports Websites Offline
content:
Two critical security flaws in PHP, the code behind most of the web, pushed hundreds of websites offline on Wednesday, October 21. Gaming and esports sites are caught up in it too, with esports wiki Liquipedia among those down for users. PHP released a fix at about 13:45 UTC (7:15 PM IST), but every site still has to install it.

The bugs, nicknamed PHP2Shell, could let attackers run their own code on a website’s server without logging in. Security agencies in Europe, the UK, Australia and Japan told site owners to patch at once or go offline until they could.

If a gaming wiki, forum or fan site you use is down today, this is the most likely reason. Expect some sites to keep flickering for the next day or two

On Tuesday evening, PHP’s security team gave advance notice of two critical bugs and a fix scheduled for 14:00 UTC Wednesday. Details had already leaked, and Cloudflare said it was seeing attack attempts.

The EU’s cyber response team, CERT-EU, then told organisations that couldn’t patch quickly to consider pulling sites offline. Agencies in the UK, Australia, Japan, Germany and the Netherlands issued similar warnings, as The Record reported .

Many listened. The Dutch parliament, government portals in Finland and France and even the Dutch cyber security centre’s own site went dark as a precaution.

title: Evil Geniuses shuts down after seven years from unsuccesful reacquisition
content:
The storied American organization follows in the footsteps of its competitor, Complexity.

Evil Geniuses, stories American esports organization, has announced the cessation of operations effective on November 6th, 2026.

The organization posted a statement by their CEO, Chris DeAppolonio, describing their effort to “stabilize operations and restore public sentiment”, ultimately succumbing to the “headwinds” of esports, including “limited sponsorships and the rising cost of competing at the top level.”

Evil Geniuses started as a Quake team in 1999, and went onto be household names in top esports such as Counter-Strike 1.6 until 2012 and Dota 2, notably winning The International in 2015.

Evil Geniuses was presided by Alex Garfield since 2004, who was a pioneer in creating sponsorship deals in esports. After being acquired by Twitch in 2014, Evil Geniuses was threatened with a boycott from other organizations due to a potential conflict of interest, impacting their ability to compete.

Evil Geniuses shifted to becoming a player-owned organization in 2016, until finally being bought by the American investment firm, PEAK6, in 2019. Under the leadership of Nicole LaPointe Jameson, Evil Geniuses initially had strong results, acquiring NRG’s Counter-Strike team that would win the final edition ESL One New York in 2019.

title: Evil Geniuses to end esports era after 27 years
content:
Esports organization Evil Geniuses just announced the end of its esports operations. The news arrived on the evening of Oct. 20, which also revealed that Evil Geniuses will shut down on Nov. 2.

Evil Geniuses will cease its competitive and day-to-day operations on Nov. 2. According to the organization’s CEO Chris DeAppolonio, the esports industry continues to face significant challenges, including limited sponsorship opportunities and rising competition costs. Despite efforts to rebuild the organization, it can no longer operate sustainably .

“Unfortunately, esports continues to face significant headwinds, including limited sponsorship and the rising cost of competing at the top level,” DeAppolonio explained. “Despite sustained investment and the dedication of the EG team, it’s been concluded that the business cannot be operated responsibly in the current environment.”

Therefore, Evil Geniuses will shut down its operations.

All players on Evil Geniuses’ esports rosters can now freely contact other organizations. Its VALORANT players and coaches will also be able to sign with new teams after the end of the 2026 season on Nov. 2.

“To the players, the staff, and everyone who put their heart and soul into EG over the last few years: you were all amazing,” DeAppolonio stated. “We gave this organization everything we had. I could not have asked for a better team. To everyone who has ever worn the EG logo, to the fans who kept showing up, and to the partners who supported this org over the last 25+ years: thank you for everything.”

title: How to get the Tactical Nuke killstreak in Modern Warfare 4
content:
The most iconic killstreak in the entire Call of Duty franchise is the Tactical Nuke, and it’s confirmed to be returning in Modern Warfare 4 . Not only was the Nuke seen in a recent MW4 trailer, but we’ve also seen gameplay of the streak in a real match.

So, naturally, this has caused players everywhere to wonder: how do you get the Nuke in Modern Warfare 4? We’ll break the killstreak down for you in the guide below.

It’s been fully confirmed that the Tactical Nuke is an earnable killstreak in Modern Warfare 4. We’ve already seen players earn the Nuke, and you call it in very similarly to other games in the Modern Warfare franchise.

The Tactical Nuke is earned when you go on a 30 killstreak in MW4. Only gun, equipment, and Field Upgrade kills count towards this streak, so you can’t factor in kills from other killstreaks. When you go on a 30 streak, you’ll get a notification that you can call in the Nuke, which immediately ends the current match and wins the game for your team . You’ll then see a unique animation play out, including your character throwing up their middle finger while being blown away by the Nuke explosion.

Just like in every other Modern Warfare game, the Tactical Nuke isn’t a killstreak that you equip as part of your three core streaks . It’s a streak that’s active for all players at all times, so whenever you go on a 30 killstreak, you’ll earn the ability to call in the Nuke.

So there you have it: the Tactical Nuke is a killstreak in Modern Warfare 4, and it’s only earned once you hit a 30 killstreak with your gun or equipment. You can’t cheese the Nuke using killstreak kills like you could in the original MW2, so it’s very rare that you’ll earn or see a Nuke called in during a match of MW4.

title: All Weapon Prestige Camos in Modern Warfare 4 & how to earn them
content:
There are several different forms of progression in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 , and one of the newer grinds in multiplayer is earning Weapon Prestige Camos. This system was brought back to the franchise in Black Ops 7, and Modern Warfare 4 has kept it in multiplayer, but with some twists.

Weapon Prestige Camos can be earned across all 33 weapons in MW4, but there are only four of them in total to unlock. You unlock each camo the same way for all weapons, but, of course, you need to know the unlock method before you start the grind. Below, we’ll explain everything you need to know about earning Weapon Prestige Camos in MW4.

The four Weapon Prestige Camos in MW4 multiplayer are: Pyroclast, Pyroclast Terminus, Pyroclast Scatter, and Pyroclast Cascade. You won’t start the process of earning any of these camos until you reach Weapon Prestige 1 with a weapon. This is accomplished by getting to that weapon’s max level, which usually goes to around 65-70 for most primary weapons.

Once you reach the max level for a weapon, you can enter Weapon Prestige , which works the same way that Classic Prestige Mode works in MW4 . When you enter Weapon Prestige, you reset that weapon back to level one and re-lock any non-shared attachments for it. You keep all shared attachments, though. From this point, you can re-unlock all weapon levels, and when you reach max level again, you’ll start earning Weapon Prestige Master levels. There are then 250 total levels to max out Weapon Prestige Master .

You can only Prestige weapons a single time in MW4, but once you do, you can start unlocking Weapon Prestige Camos. Look below to find out what you need to do to unlock all four Weapon Prestige Camos in multiplayer:

Unlike in Black Ops 7, which has unique Weapon Prestige Camos for every single weapon, the four camos are the same for all weapons in Modern Warfare 4. So, just because you earn Pyroclast Cascade for the M4 doesn’t then mean you have it unlocked for the Patriot XMR. Every Weapon Prestige grind is separate, but the Weapon Prestige Camos are the same.

title: Best Permanent Unlocks to spend Tokens on in Modern Warfare 4
content:
Classic Prestige has returned in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, and that means that Permanent Unlock Tokens are coming back as well. If you’re unfamiliar with how Prestige Mode works, it resets your level back to one, but you receive a Permanent Unlock Token that you can use on any class item in multiplayer in exchange.

This is a huge benefit, as it lets you permanently unlock an item so you never have to unlock it again during the entire Prestige grind in Modern Warfare 4 . However, with so many items to choose from, which unlock gives you the best bang for your buck?

Below, we’ll give you five distinct class items in MW4 multiplayer that are most worth spending a Permanent Unlock Token on after you Prestige. The item list is in order from 1-5.

First on the list has to be the Stim, which is a piece of Tactical Equipment that quickly heals you back to full health when applied. The Stim is unlocked at level 47 in MW4 multiplayer, making it one of the final items you’ll unlock every single Prestige.

While there are other solid pieces of Tactical Equipment you can use until that level, once you get used to the Stim, there’s really no going back. The ability to get back into the fight instantly after being injured, compared to waiting for several seconds to recoup health, is one of the most important benefits of any item in multiplayer. If you use a Permanent Unlock Token on the Stim, your Tactical slot is pretty much set in stone on all loadouts in multiplayer.

Next up, we have the Axion assault rifle, which is unlocked at level 52. The Axion is one of the best assault rifles in Modern Warfare 4, and having it available for only three levels every Prestige is ultimately a waste of its potential. This is arguably a top meta weapon in multiplayer, so you’ll want it permanently unlocked as soon as possible.

title: How to level up weapons faster in Modern Warfare 4
content:
Weapon leveling is one of the core elements in any Call of Duty, but the 33 total weapons in Modern Warfare 4 have dozens of levels that you need to grind through. While it will take a long time before you reach max level with all weapons, or even your favorites, there are some key tips you can take advantage of to make the leveling process much less stressful. To see the best ways to level up your weapons quickly in Modern Warfare 4, keep reading the guide below.

We’ll lay out some distinct, fast weapon leveling methods for Modern Warfare 4, but they will mostly be tied to multiplayer.

It’s one of the most common ways to earn more XP in Call of Duty, but that’s because it simply works the best. While you can certainly get more overall XP by playing objective game modes, this also applies to weapon XP.

The more XP you earn during the course of a match, the more XP is applied to the weapon that you’re currently using. So, while kills still offer the most weapon XP possible, playing the objective and earning match score that way also grants you weapon XP.

The best objective modes to play if you want to earn weapon XP faster than any other method are Kill Confirmed, Hardpoint, and Domination , but the first two are going to be your best bets. When playing Kill Confirmed, make sure you’re picking up any dog tag possible for the max amount of XP, while in Hardpoint you want to continually attack the hill, getting kills in and around it for extra XP.

As long as you’re primarily using the weapon you want to level up fast in Modern Warfare 4, you’ll get a ton of regular and weapon XP in objective game modes.

Après avoir brillé sur la scène internationale en 2026, shxrk et t3eny tenteront désormais de franchir la dernière marche avec Peterbot. Sur le papier, l’association réunit trois joueurs capables de rivaliser avec les meilleurs, mais leur complémentarité reste à démontrer. L’arrivée d’une nouvelle personnalité au sein d’un duo déjà bien établi pourrait notamment nécessiter quelques ajustements dans leur manière de jouer.

Si certains observateurs s’interrogent sur la capacité des trois joueurs à évoluer ensemble, Clix ne partage pas ces inquiétudes. Le streamer et joueur américain s’est montré particulièrement enthousiaste à l’annonce de cette association. « Je ne vois pas comment ce trio pourrait ne pas fonctionner. Les trois sont capables de s’adapter les uns aux autres » , a-t-il déclaré.

De son côté, Swizzy pourrait également retrouver une équipe de premier plan. Double champion du monde en titre, il serait désormais susceptible de rejoindre Vic0 et Malibuca, une autre association qui pourrait faire parler d’elle lors des prochaines FNCS. Cette piste reste toutefois à confirmer.

Avec Peterbot, shxrk et t3eny réunis sous les mêmes couleurs, la saison 2027 de Fortnite s’annonce déjà particulièrement intéressante. Reste à voir si ce trio parviendra à transformer son immense potentiel individuel en résultats collectifs, avec un objectif évident : décrocher le titre mondial.

title: All Prestige Icons in Modern Warfare 4 multiplayer
content:
One of the best decisions that Call of Duty has made over the past two years has been bringing back Classic Prestige, and that popular feature is back in Modern Warfare 4 . While Prestige does work a little differently this year, as there are two Prestige options for players, what hasn’t changed are the Prestige Icons that players can earn in Modern Warfare 4.

Naturally, the Prestige Icons look completely new compared to any game before MW4, but the way you earn them is the same. You enter Prestige Mode after reaching level 55 and reset your level, but you earn an icon next to your name and some other exclusive rewards. If you’re curious about the Prestige Icons, we have a complete view of what they look like in MW4, and you can see them in the guide below.

In total, there are 10 Prestige Icons that players can earn in multiplayer, along with a Prestige Master icon. We haven’t seen the Prestige Master icon just yet, but we do have a look at all 10 of the standard Prestige Icons available in MW4.

As you can see from the 10 icons, there are some clear callbacks to previous Call of Duty games represented on most of the icons. For example, Prestige 6 has the COD Ghosts logo, while Prestige 7 has the Infinite Warfare logo. We also see Prestige 5 feature the silhouette of the Modern Warfare 3 (2011) soldier logo. Prestige 10 features the “4” icon from MW4 as well, so most Infinity Ward CODs are showcased in some fashion.

It should also be noted that the individual Prestige Icons are animated. The golden figures in the middle of each icon move in unique ways, and this can be seen in-game.

While these Prestige Icons might be more monochromatic than some players might have liked, the different logos and symbols in each of the icons are nice throwbacks for Call of Duty veterans. The icons being animated is also a nice touch, as the past two years in BO6 and BO7 have featured static icons.

title: All confirmed weapons in Modern Warfare 4 so far
content:
Every Call of Duty title is built on key gameplay elements, and weapons are right at the forefront. Weapons can either make or break a game, and in Modern Warfare 4 , you’ll have access to 33 guns, launchers, and melee weapons to dispatch your enemies.

While we’ve seen a solid amount of weapons already in Modern Warfare 4, there are quite a few that have never been seen before. Luckily, we’ve rounded up every officially and unofficially revealed gun so far, giving you a complete look at the Modern Warfare 4 weapons list ahead of its release date in October.

In the multiplayer beta for Modern Warfare 4, there were over 20 weapons available to unlock and use. Of course, this doesn’t leave a lot of room for weapons at launch, given there are only around 33 expected in the game on Oct. 23. However, we already have a solid idea of what the unconfirmed weapons will be thanks to data miners going into the game files and uncovering their names and models.

The Oden is currently the only unconfirmed assault rifle we know of, but it’s been found in the game files , so it appears it’s coming to MW4 at launch. The rest of the ARs were playable in the multiplayer beta.

title: RLCS : la pépite solar débarque chez Spacestation (off.)
content:
Spacestation Gaming tient sa troisième recrue pour les RLCS 2027. L’organisation nord-américaine a annoncé la signature de Rexton « solar » M., jeune talent de 17 ans qui évoluera aux côtés de Jack « reveal » LeDuc et Zachary « zach » Stone, sous les ordres du coach André « Xpere » Ruivinho. Il prendra la place laissée vacante par le Brésilien diaz, contraint de quitter l’équipe en raison de complications administratives liées à son visa. Ce dernier est désormais pressenti chez Vitality, où il pourrait retrouver nass et Oski.

Le recrutement de solar constitue une véritable surprise. Repéré grâce à son ascension fulgurante dans les classements en ligne, l’Américain n’a encore jamais disputé de Main Event RLCS. Il a néanmoins montré des qualités prometteuses en terminant dans le Top 12 du Last Chance Qualifier nord-américain aux côtés de Druee et Kehvn. Il a également atteint la phase suisse des Opens 1v1 et 2v2 de sa région, avec deux Top 22 à la clé. Initialement attendu chez 9Lives avec monk et Juice, il a finalement choisi de rejoindre Spacestation Gaming.

Ce choix s’inscrit dans la tradition de Spacestation Gaming, réputée pour avoir révélé plusieurs jeunes talents nord-américains, notamment Daniel, Sypical et Arsenal. Mais solar devra rapidement faire ses preuves au sein d’une équipe qui sort d’une saison 2026 exceptionnelle. Après un Top 8 au Major de Paris, SSG a enchaîné deux finales internationales, à l’Esports World Cup puis aux championnats du monde RLCS, s’inclinant à chaque fois face à Team Falcons.

Avec reveal et zach comme coéquipiers, solar aura donc la lourde tâche de succéder à diaz et de maintenir Spacestation Gaming parmi les meilleures formations mondiales. Un immense défi pour un joueur de 17 ans qui s’apprête à découvrir le plus haut niveau, avec le Club Championship 2027 en ligne de mire.
